Pages you visit in this tab are kept out of your history, and session cookies are cleared when the last private tab closes.
This is not anonymity. Your network, your internet provider and the sites you visit can still see your traffic. ReWeb has no VPN and does not hide your address.

Delete all %1$d history entries? This cannot be undone.

ReWeb saves APK files but never installs them. Open the file to let Android’s installer handle it.
Storage permission is required to save downloads on this version of Android
This link cannot be downloaded: unsupported address type

This file is generated inside the page (a blob: link). ReWeb cannot download it — the data never leaves the page, and reading it would require giving every website access to the app. Try the site’s own “save” or “export” option.
Android’s download service is disabled on this device. Enable “Download Manager” in app settings.
The download could not be started
ReWeb does not remember camera, microphone or location answers — sites must ask every time. Protected media playback is remembered for this site, because players fail if asked repeatedly.
Android denied the permission, so the site was denied too
ReWeb could not verify that this is really %1$s. %2$s
If you continue, anything you send to this site could be read or changed by someone else. Do not continue to enter passwords or payment details.
The site’s certificate is not valid yet.
The certificate was issued for a different address.
The certificate was not issued by an authority this device trusts.
The certificate’s dates are invalid. Check that this device’s clock is correct — a wrong date is the most common cause on older phones.
The certificate could not be validated.

This is almost certainly this device, not the site. Android 7.0 and older shipped their list of trusted certificate authorities in the system image, and it is never updated. That list does not include ISRG Root X1, the authority behind Let\'s Encrypt, which secures a large part of the web — so many perfectly legitimate sites now fail here.\n\nYou can fix this permanently: download the ISRG Root X1 certificate from letsencrypt.org/certificates (the self-signed DER or PEM file), then install it through Settings → Security → Install from storage. ReWeb trusts certificates you install yourself, the same way Chrome does.
Continue to %1$s without a verified certificate? This lasts until you close ReWeb.
This device is not connected to a network.
Check Wi-Fi or mobile data, then try again.
ReWeb could not find the server for %1$s.
Check the spelling of the address. If it is correct, the site’s DNS may be down or blocked on this network.
The server may be down, or a firewall on this network may be blocking it.
The connection to %1$s was closed before the page finished loading.
This is usually a flaky network. Try again; if it keeps happening on mobile data, try Wi-Fi.
The network may be slow or the server overloaded. Try again in a moment.
ReWeb could not establish an encrypted connection to %1$s.

On older Android versions this usually means the site requires newer encryption than this device supports, or the device’s date is wrong. Updating Android System WebView from the Play Store can help; the device clock is worth checking first.
%1$s kept redirecting and never arrived at a page.
This often clears up after deleting the site’s cookies in Settings → Privacy.
ReWeb does not know how to open this type of address.
If this link is meant for another app, that app may not be installed.
%1$s does not have a page at this address.
The link may be out of date. Try the site’s home page.
%1$s is temporarily refusing requests from this device.
Wait a few minutes before trying again.
%1$s returned an error instead of a page.
This is a problem on the site, not on this device. Try again later.
Something went wrong while loading %1$s, and the engine did not say what.
Try reloading. If it keeps failing, check Diagnostics to see whether this device’s WebView supports the site.
This page ran out of memory
The rendering engine stopped while displaying %1$s.
Heavy pages can exceed what this device can hold. Closing other tabs before reloading usually helps.
The system WebView is unavailable. It may be updating — try again shortly.
This device’s browser engine is too old for this site
%1$s needs browser features that Android System WebView on this device does not provide. The installed engine reports Chromium %2$s.
This is a limitation of this device, not of ReWeb. Updating “Android System WebView” from the Play Store is the only fix, and on some older devices no newer version is offered.
This device’s WebView is Chromium %1$s. Some modern sites will not work correctly.
Opens in its own window, separate from your tabs. It shares your cookies and sign-ins with normal browsing — installing is not a privacy boundary.
Only http and https pages can be installed
No web apps installed.\n\nOpen a site, then choose “Install web app” from the menu.
Remove “%1$s”? Your cookies and sign-in for the site are kept.
The template must start with http(s):// and contain %s
Required by most modern sites. Turning it off saves memory but breaks them.
Turn off to save data and memory on slow connections
History, cookies, cache and site storage
Offer to open sign-in pages in another browser
Google and other providers refuse to sign you in inside an embedded browser. See Diagnostics for what this can and cannot do.
ReWeb stores everything on this device. There is no account, no sync and no server.
These tests run real code inside this device’s WebView. A result of UNKNOWN means the capability could not be measured — it is not reported as passing.
This WebView predates the baseline modern sites are built for (Chromium %1$d). Breakage on such sites is expected on this device.
This WebView is recent enough for most modern sites.
The Chromium version could not be determined.
This device shipped without ISRG Root X1, but you have installed it yourself, so Let\'s Encrypt sites work normally. Nothing further is needed.

This device\'s list of trusted certificate authorities is part of its system image and is never updated. It predates ISRG Root X1, the Let\'s Encrypt root, so many legitimate HTTPS sites — Wikipedia among them — will report an untrusted certificate. This is independent of the WebView version: the engine can be modern while the trust store is not.\n\nFix: download ISRG Root X1 from letsencrypt.org/certificates and install it via Settings → Security → Install from storage. ReWeb trusts certificates you install yourself.
This device has no Widevine support at all, so no protected streaming service can play here in any browser or app.

The platform itself can use Widevine. If the browser checks below still fail, the limitation is in this device\'s WebView rather than in its DRM hardware — and no app-side change can work around that, because a browser cannot supply its own content decryption module.
Widevine is present but could not be used: %1$s
Opens the site in a new tab so you can see how it behaves on this device. ReWeb has no special handling for any of them.
This looks like a sign-in that redirects back to ReWeb. Opening it in another browser is more likely to work, and you will be returned here when it finishes.

This looks like a sign-in page. Providers such as Google refuse to sign you in inside an embedded browser.\n\nOpening it in another browser will let the sign-in succeed there, but the resulting session stays in that browser — Android does not let apps share cookies, so you may still not be signed in here.
No other browser is installed on this device, so the sign-in has to run here. It may be refused by the provider.
